title: OpenTensor reduction Square
statement: Under the original finite-type family, structural-square and admissibility hypotheses, Assertion holds for the openTensor generator whenever both endpoint words have length at most three. The normalized operation models are those of [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge] and the typed-word domain is that of [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain]; the operation data, finite words, generator kinds, admissibility predicates and the coefficient-square Assertion are those of [def-sf-generator-reduction-data]. This is only this forward generator case; it asserts neither the other three generators nor inverse-square or naturality clauses. StructuralSquares is the predicate of [def-sf-open-interchange-reduction-data].

proof.text: Use the ordinary word comparison q of TensorAdjunctionReductionSquares. The existing word_completion_reduction identity gives R(completionMap_B) followed by r_B = q_B. On the stipulated endpoint length/admissibility domain completionMap_B is invertible, so assertion_of_ordinary_square reduces the goal to the ordinary ringed projection square.

proof.text: The ordinary pullback/reduction tensor square is canonicalReductionPullTensor. The inverse open coefficient comparison is the inverse mate of reductionPull, and its components are invertible by canonicalOpenReduction_isIso. The inverse-mate unit and counit identities therefore give its open-adjunction squares. Expand both inverse projection formulas through their prescribed transpose fields. Tensor naturality, the unit square and the restriction/tensor square show compatibility of their transposes. Apply open extension, use naturality of the inverse open mate, and paste the counit square. This proves the primitive inverse projection square without any word-length restriction.

proof.text: Insert the ordinary child comparisons q_B,q_C by naturality of the system inverse projection isomorphism and bifunctoriality of tensor. The resulting inverse square is the reverse of the ordinary forward-generator square. Cancel the inverse system projection and the inverse ringed projection. Finally apply the completion transport of step 1. Every equality is a whole-system equality, before any finite evaluation.

theorem openTensorReductionSquare
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} (Cf : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic Cf.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic Cf.l) E] (o : Operations Cf.l E)
    (hStructural : StructuralSquares.{u, s, i} Cf.l E D o)
    {S : Type s} (W : S → Scheme.{u}) (hW : FiniteTypeFamily W D.k)
    {I : Type i} (location : I → S)
    {a b : S} (j : W a ⟶ W b) (hj : IsOpenImmersion j)
      (hq : QuasiCompact j) (B : Word W location a) (C : Word W location b)
    (hSourceLength : (Word.tensor (Word.open j hj hq B) C).length ≤ 3)
    (hTargetLength : (Word.open j hj hq (Word.tensor B (Word.pull j (by let := hj; infer_instance)
          (by let := hj; infer_instance) hq C))).length ≤ 3)
    (K : ∀ k : I, DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource Cf.l E (W (location k))))
    (lo hi torLo torHi : ℤ)
    (hInputs : ∀ k : I, Admissible Cf.l E
      (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus Cf.l E (W (location k))) (K k)
      lo hi torLo torHi)
    (hSource : Word.admissible Cf.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi
      (Word.tensor
      (Word.open j hj hq B) C))
    (hTarget : Word.admissible Cf.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi
      (Word.open j hj hq
      (Word.tensor B
      (Word.pull j (by let := hj; infer_instance)
          (by let := hj; infer_instance) hq C))))
    (hGenerator : GeneratorKind.admissible Cf.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi
      (GeneratorKind.openTensor j hj hq B C)) :
    Assertion Cf.l E W location o K (GeneratorKind.openTensor j hj hq B C)
